name: bonk-sir-jump
notes: Sir Bonk jump (anim.jump), 2026-10-21: squat, hero-leap launch, ease into the fall loop (exit = sirfall tick 0).
character: Sir Bonk (68 joints: a Humanoid body with Mixamo names and full fingers; a 3x4 cape chain Cape_L/C/R1..4 under Spine2 that a spring drives in the game, so leave it at rest; a 2.26 m wooden plank greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0, bladeHilt where its 1.42 m blade leaves the crossguard and bladeEnd at the tip)
description:
Sir Bonk's jump: the clip he plays when he jumps, from the jump squat through the rise to the top of the jump, where the game crossfades into his fall loop. A double jump plays it again in the air. Every aerial attack and his fall start from where this jump takes him.

Who he is. Sir Bonk is a huge, good-hearted, slightly dumb brute who read Don Quixote once and knighted himself (images 1 and 2). He has a blue mop-bucket helm with a broom crest, a cream tabard with his painted crown, pot-lid pauldrons and a cape, and he carries a plank greatsword. He believes he is the hero of the story: proud and determined, chest out, chin up. His idle holds the plank on his right shoulder with the left fist on his hip, and he runs like a proud charge with the plank still on the shoulder.

How the game plays it. Ticks 0-36 at 60 Hz (0.6 s), played once. Tick 0 is his idle pose exactly; the game crossfades into the jump from the idle or the run over 0.05 s. Ticks 0-4 are the jump squat on the ground, and the game launches him at tick 4. A full jump rises until about tick 34 (3.25 m up). Then the game crossfades over 0.15 s into the fall loop, so ticks 34-36 must be exactly the fall's first pose (reference 'sirfall', tick 0, given as `b.exit_pose`). A short hop reaches its top at about tick 21 and a double jump at about tick 24 (played from tick 0, in the air), so by tick 20 he should already be easing toward the fall pose. The fighter does not move in the clip: the game carries him up. Keep the hips 0-20 cm below the idle's through the whole clip (the air references sit 11-20 cm below). The match camera sits behind and above him.

The jump, the hero leap:
- Ticks 0-4, the squat: a quick, heavy dip. The hips drop 10-16 cm, the knees bend 40-60 degrees and the chest folds 10-15 degrees forward. The left fist leaves his hip and swings down and back, winding up. The plank stays on the shoulder while the right arm compresses with the body. The head stays up, eyes ahead. The deepest point is tick 3-4. Tick 0 is his approved idle, whose plank hand is folded back about 137 degrees off the forearm (hidden behind the plank). Straighten that wrist during the squat, by tick 4, by turning the forearm and moving the elbow while the plank stays on the shoulder; from tick 4 on the wrist stays under 45 degrees. The check skips ticks 0-3 for that wrist.
- Ticks 4-9, the launch: explosive. The left leg drives him up: it straightens (knee bent 20 degrees or less) and its toes point down. The right knee drives up in front (thigh 60-80 degrees forward, knee bent 90-120 degrees). The left fist punches straight up to the sky, the arm nearly straight and the fist above the head and a little forward: the hero's "to the rescue!". The chest lifts and opens, leaning back a few degrees, chin up.
- Ticks 9-20, the rise: he holds the hero leap. The fist overshoots a little and settles, the plank lags behind the body and settles 2-4 ticks later, and the head stays steady.
- Ticks 20-34: he eases into the fall pose (`b.exit_pose`). The fist comes down and out to his side for balance, the left leg relaxes into its hanging pose, the chest leans forward 5-12 degrees and he looks ahead and a little down.
- The plank stays resting on the right shoulder throughout, at the angle of his idle and fall: the right hand at chest height in front of the shoulder and clear of the bucket, the plank rising steeply over the shoulder with the tip high above the hilt and out to his right, so the match camera behind him sees the whole plank, never end-on. It stays clear of the head, the crest, the cape and the raised fist.

Fast motion belongs to the launch only (ticks 2-9). Use Clip.overlap() for follow-through. Do not animate the cape joints (Cape_L/C/R1..4): a spring drives them in the game, so leave them at their rest rotation. No props other than the plank, no spins and no attack. Keep each hand in line with its forearm (wrists under 45 degrees).
